theme: Doctrinal Pause: The Means of Grace, Word, Sacrament, Prayer
doctrine: The Means of Grace, Word, Sacrament, Prayer
summary: How God ordinarily strengthens his people, through the preached Word, the sacraments, and prayer
readingInstruction: Read Acts 2:42 and Romans 10:14-17. Today is a doctrinal pause on the means of grace: the ordinary ways God works in his people. Notice the four things the first church devoted itself to, and how Paul explains that faith comes by hearing.
settingTheScene: After three thousand are added to the church at Pentecost, Luke gives a one-verse summary of what they did together. Paul, in Romans 10, explains why preaching is essential: no one can call on a Lord they have not heard about. The church has long called the means by which God gives and increases grace “the means of grace”. The Reformers summarized them as the Word, the sacraments (baptism and the Lord’s Supper), and prayer.
observation: “And they devoted themselves to the apostles” teaching and the fellowship’ (Acts 2:42).
“To the breaking of bread and the prayers” (Acts 2:42).
“For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved” (Romans 10:13).
“How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard?” (Romans 10:14).
“And how are they to hear without someone preaching?” (Romans 10:14).
“And how are they to preach unless they are sent?” (Romans 10:15).
“How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news!” (Romans 10:15).
“So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ” (Romans 10:17).
doctrinalFocus: The means of grace are the ordinary channels through which God gives his people his blessing, strengthens their faith, and conforms them to Christ. They are not magic, and they do not work apart from faith and the Holy Spirit. But God has promised to use them. The Reformed tradition names three main means: the Word, the sacraments, and prayer. The Word, read and preached, is the primary means. “Faith comes from hearing” (Romans 10:17). The Spirit uses the Scriptures to convict, to convert, and to sanctify. The sacraments are the signs and seals of the gospel, instituted by Christ: baptism, which marks entrance into the covenant community, and the Lord’s Supper, in which believers feed on Christ by faith. Christians differ on how Christ is present in the Supper and on who should be baptized, but all agree that these are gifts to be received with faith. Prayer is the response to God’s Word and the believer’s way of seeking him. To these, Acts 2:42 adds fellowship, the life together in which believers encourage and build up one another. The means of grace are meant to be practiced in the context of a local church. They remind us that the Christian life is not a solo project. God gives grace through a people, a book, a meal, and a prayer.
interpretation:
Acts 2:42 is a short portrait of a healthy church. They “devoted themselves,” a word that means persistent, steadfast commitment. They did not drop in occasionally. First, “the apostles” teaching.’ The church was built on the teaching of those who had been with Jesus, now preserved in the New Testament. Second, “the fellowship,” the sharing of life, resources, and burdens that grows out of a shared faith. Third, “the breaking of bread,” which likely includes shared meals and the Lord’s Supper. Fourth, “the prayers,” both private and corporate.

Notice that these are ordinary things. There is no mention of a new program or a special technique. God works through ordinary means: teaching, fellowship, meals, and prayer. This is encouraging. You do not need extraordinary experiences to grow. You need to be steadily present in these four things.

Romans 10 makes the case for why the Word matters so much. Paul builds a chain of questions. People cannot call on the Lord unless they believe. They cannot believe unless they have heard. They cannot hear unless someone preaches. They cannot preach unless they are sent. So salvation depends on the proclamation of the gospel. “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news!” Then the summary: “Faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.” The word is not a mere pointer to something else. The Spirit works through it.

This is why time in the Word matters. You are putting yourself under the Word. It is also the reason that gathering with a church matters. You hear the Word preached, you pray with others, and you receive the sacraments. These are not extras. They are how God has chosen to feed his people.
connection: Deuteronomy 8:3 says man lives by every word from the mouth of God. Isaiah 55:10-11 says God’s word accomplishes his purpose. Matthew 28:19-20 commands baptism and teaching. Luke 22:19 and 1 Corinthians 11:23-26 institute the Lord’s Supper. Hebrews 10:24-25 calls us not to neglect meeting together. Colossians 3:16 says to let the word of Christ dwell richly. 1 Peter 2:2 says to long for the pure spiritual milk. Ephesians 4:11-16 describes the building up of the church.
application:
Evaluate your own pattern against the four: teaching, fellowship, bread, prayer. Which is weakest?

Commit to regular attendance at your church. Treat it as a means of grace, not an option.

Thank someone who first brought you the gospel. Their feet were beautiful.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the ordinary means of grace: his Word, the sacraments, and prayer.
Ask him to make you faithful in using them.
Ask him to meet you through them.
